title: Bluetooth re-enables
line: Bluetooth that you turned off no longer turns itself back on after resume.
explanation: Every time an adapter appears (at login, and again when it re-registers after resume or a firmware reset), bluedevil's kded restores its powered state one second later in DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter(). That read the saved state with a default of on, and since Bluetooth being disabled clears the saved adapter states, an adapter re-appearing while Bluetooth was off got powered back on. The 2025 fix (76da3998) only covered restoreState(), not this path. Now restoreAdapter() only sets the powered state when one was saved for that adapter, like restoreState().

commits.message:
kded: don't power on adapters with no saved state when they appear

When an adapter showed up, for example again after resume, its powered
state was restored with a default of on, so Bluetooth that the user had
disabled came back. Only restore it when a state was saved for it.

BUG: 507836

patches.diff:
From 117610e52a24f8b824f1efd0c518c9c7ab28a24d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:33:08 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] kded: don't power on adapters with no saved state when they
 appear

When an adapter showed up, for example again after resume, its powered
state was restored with a default of on, so Bluetooth that the user had
disabled came back. Only restore it when a state was saved for it.

BUG: 507836
---
 src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp | 5 ++++-
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp b/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
index 1de54443..f78fc2b8 100644
--- a/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
+++ b/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
@@ -216,7 +216,10 @@ void DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter(BluezQt::AdapterPtr adapter)
     KConfigGroup adaptersGroup = GlobalSettings::self()->config()->group("Adapters");
 
     const QString &key = QStringLiteral("%1_powered").arg(adapter->address());
-    adapter->setPowered(adaptersGroup.readEntry<bool>(key, true));
+
+    if (adaptersGroup.hasKey(key)) {
+        adapter->setPowered(adaptersGroup.readEntry<bool>(key, true));
+    }
 }
 
 void DeviceMonitor::clearPlaces()
-- 
2.53.0

review.text: Directly completes commit 76da3998 by applying the same adaptersGroup.hasKey(key) guard to DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter() that was previously added to restoreState(). This closes the exact resume/adapter-reappearance path that caused the bug to be reopened when Bluetooth was disabled and saved adapter states were cleared. Verification with dbusmock BlueZ covers both the disabled-resume bug and the remembered-adapter regression case.

reviews.text: Directly completes commit 76da3998 by applying the same adaptersGroup.hasKey(key) guard to DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter() that was previously added to restoreState(). This closes the exact resume/adapter-reappearance path that caused the bug to be reopened when Bluetooth was disabled and saved adapter states were cleared. Verification with dbusmock BlueZ covers both the disabled-resume bug and the remembered-adapter regression case.

restoreAdapter() powering adapters on with a default of true is a real hole left by 76da3998, and the hasKey() guard closes it when no state is saved, as the before/after logs show. But the saved [Adapters] keys are only cleared by saveState(), which runs at login with launchState=disable/enable, on suspend and at kded shutdown. It does not run when the user turns Bluetooth off in the applet or KCM. In the reporter's original flow (c0: Bluetooth was on, they turned it off in the KCM, sleep is disabled, it came back after a screen unlock), the keys from the previous logout still say powered=true, so a re-appearing adapter would still be powered on by this patch. The test only covers the case where the group is already empty.
changes: In restoreAdapter() also return early when Bluetooth is currently blocked (m_manager->isBluetoothBlocked()), or clear/update the saved adapter state when bluetoothBlockedChanged fires.
Re-test with launchState=remember, a saved <addr>_powered=true, then Bluetooth disabled at runtime (setBluetoothBlocked(true) via the KCM path) and the adapter re-added: it must stay off.
